records.failureSummary: Added AC-numbered unit tests for parseDuration in test/duration.test.mjs, following the existing project convention (node:test + node:assert/strict, auto-discovered by node --test / npm test). The 8 new tests [AC-01]..[AC-08] cover FR-1..FR-5 and TS-7 plus boundaries: single-unit conversion 1h/30m/45s/250ms (AC-01); aggregation 1h30m (AC-02); case/space 1H 30M and 1h 30m (AC-03); unitless 500 (AC-04); invalid inputs '' / whitespace-only / 1x / -1h / 1.5h / 1h1h all explicitly asserted === null (AC-05); out-of-order 30m1h (AC-06); non-string inputs null/undefined/250/{} === null (AC-07); assert.doesNotThrow over all invalid inputs incl. non-strings (AC-08). Red-first was demonstrated for real: the identical test file run against a stub parseDuration that throws (the pre-implementation behavior) failed 11/11 (tests 11, pass 0, fail 11, exit 1), with AC-08 failing as an unwanted-exception assertion; the stub lived only in a scratch dir (/tmp, since removed) and no product code was modified. Against the shipped implementation the suite is green: node --test and npm run test both report tests 11, pass 11, fail 0, errors 0, exit 0. npm run build and npm run lint (node --check src/duration.mjs) also exit 0. fixTaskType: none (no product-code fix required; the only genuine failure was the intentional red-first run, resolved by the existing implementation).
